model_name: HistGradientBoosting+sigmoid_calibration (OPTUNA-TUNED hyperparameters, 33 features incl. catalog crowding, stellar variability, Gaia DR3 astrometry)
updated_by: optuna_deploy_retrain.py (hyperparameters only; feature set unchanged at 33)
note: Hyperparameter-only change. Resampled over 12 training bootstraps: +0.0045 (sd 0.0015), CI [+0.0024, +0.0070], positive 12/12, at/above MDE 0/12 (max single resample +0.0075 vs MDE 0.0097). Brier 0.0763 -> 0.0739, ECE 0.0355 -> 0.0338. THIS DID NOT CLEAR THE STANDING PROMOTION BAR, which requires ci_lo > 0 AND mean delta >= MDE (0.0097); only the first leg was met. Promoted anyway as an explicit, user-authorised exception on the strength of 12/12 positive resamples, a CI excluding zero, simultaneous Brier and ECE improvement, and no evidence of search overfitting (nested-CV delta was SMALLER than the resampled-test delta). CatBoost (+0.0080) and trap_vshape remain correctly unpromoted under the same rule; the bar is unchanged for future proposals.
raw_lightcurve_dependency: var_* features are computed from RAW pre-flatten light curves (data/known_lightcurves*, data/unknown_lightcurves*, data/retrain_pipeline/raw), NOT data/processed*. 02_preprocess.py savgol-flattens over ~13.4 h, which removes the multi-day rotational signal these features measure. See code/experiments/variability_features.py.
hyperparameter_provenance: Optuna TPE, 120 trials/fold, outer-5/inner-3 nested CV; selected by the final full-training study in optuna_hpo_nested.json. This is NOT the pre-Gaia 'legacy tuned' config (lr 0.1 / iter 500 / leaves 63 / l2 0.5 / balanced), which was separately tested at 33 features and measured +0.0016 with a CI spanning zero, and it is NOT sklearn defaults (lr 0.1 / iter 100 / leaves 31 / l2 0.0 / cw None), which is what was actually deployed from the Gaia swap until now.
promotion_rule_status: DELIBERATE EXCEPTION -- DID NOT CLEAR THE MDE
training_cost_note: Fitting is ~9.7x more expensive than the previous default config (475 boosting iterations at 63 leaves vs 100 at 31): 3.5s -> 34.1s for a single full-training fit on a clean 8-core machine. This affects RETRAIN wall-clock only. Inference is 4.7x slower in RELATIVE terms (0.0659s -> 0.307s to score the 1,098-row frozen test) but negligible in ABSOLUTE terms: 0.28 ms per star, so scoring the entire 254-candidate ranked pool costs ~0.07s versus ~0.015s before. Serving latency is not a practical concern at this scale, but it is NOT unchanged -- the ratio is real and would matter if the scored pool grew by orders of magnitude. The 32-member bootstrap uncertainty ensemble inherits the same ~10x training cost and is the most expensive downstream rebuild.
